rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (kp 1.6, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.1, 5 sensors at x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05, sensor_size 0.012) remains the best raced design at 511.25. Iteration 8 tested kp 1.4 with everything else fixed and scored 489.44. The oval stayed 20/20 and slalom progress was marginally higher (0.175 vs 0.171), but s-bend finishes fell from 5/20 to 3/20 and s-bend max_error stayed at 0.0605 m. That is a net loss, so kp 1.4 is rejected and kp returns to 1.6. Across the tests, s-bend max_error has sat at 0.060 to 0.063 m under every speed (1.3, 1.1, 1.0), damping (kd 0.5 to 1.0) and proportional gain (1.4, 1.6) setting. The controller levers now appear exhausted, so the remaining untested lever is the sensor footprint. Change: sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016, the only edit to the best design (kp 1.6, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, last_direction, sensor_weights -2..2). A larger footprint covers more of the tape at each sensor, so the robot should see the line earlier on bends and read the tape more smoothly, and the 0.03 m spacing still leaves no gaps. Expected result: s-bend finishes rise above 5/20 and max_error drops below 0.06 m, with the oval staying at 20/20 near 2.0 s. Risks: a wider footprint blurs the signal and could increase oscillation on the oval, or lower the signal's peak on tight corners. Fallback: if the oval drops below 20/20, or slalom progress falls below 0.171, return sensor_size to 0.012 (the iteration 6 design). Hypotheses to check: (1) the s-bend bend limit is set by how early the sensors see the tape, not by gain or speed; (2) the flat max_error across controller settings points to sensing. Geometry positions are not changed, because the iteration 2 spacing and y 0.07 layout scored 62.76.
